archive_04_public_001.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_001.text: Luo began the public access report with a locked cupboard and a question he disliked. How many people had come last winter and gone away without receiving the record they needed? The ordinary visitor book listed completed consultations carefully. Refusals occupied a separate pile of notes, some filed by date and others by the document requested. Yue divided them without joining names across unrelated matters. The number of successful readers would not describe the people missing from the reading room, but counting refusals was less simple than counting empty chairs.

archive_04_public_002.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_002.text: The first bundle contained a mountain widow's request for a certified road allowance. She had received the required extract after six days, by which time the departing cart had already left. The archive had marked the consultation complete. Luo remembered it and said the delay had concerned a missing registrar comparison, not a closed table. Yue recorded both facts. The woman had eventually received the document; she had also paid for another journey. A correct paper arriving too late could turn a successful entry into a practical failure.

archive_04_public_003.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_003.text: The second refusal involved a private family letter whose owner declined consultation. Luo had thought the refusal harsh because the requester hoped to identify a deceased father. Dai's note recorded an offered alternative: a public marriage register with the relevant names, which the requester consulted that afternoon. Yue placed the episode in a different column from the delayed allowance. Refusal of one source had not meant abandonment of the request. Luo looked uncomfortable, then asked her to leave the episode visible. His argument for opening hours could survive an example of protected privacy helping someone.

archive_04_public_004.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_04_public_004.text: I once wrote that a locked door is always a cost. I still think it can be. But if I use that sentence to make every owner explain herself to every visitor, I have built a different locked room around the owner. Put the alternative consultation in the report. I want the winter hall open because people need its public records, not because I have discovered a grand reason to dislike keys. Dai will enjoy hearing me say that. Perhaps we can spare her the exact words.

archive_04_public_005.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_005.text: They examined travel times next. Winter readers often came from a village whose safe cart arrived after the advertised morning consultation ended. Extending one afternoon would serve them better than adding another early hour. The village carter had already sent the seasonal timetable with his road licence. Yue compared it to the archive's opening notice and saw the mismatch plainly. Luo had copied last year's notice after a clerk retired. The carter had changed his route to avoid a broken bridge. Neither institution had asked what the other change required.

archive_04_public_006.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_006.text: Luo invited the carter's appointed booking clerk to the ordinary planning meeting. The clerk arrived carrying a timetable board rather than a petition. She could offer a Tuesday afternoon arrival while the road stayed open, but no promise for snowbound weeks. She wanted a covered waiting place where passengers could sit if the reading tables filled. The archive's yard roof could shelter two benches after the beam materials moved. Dai approved assessing the space. Yue copied a schedule that named its weather dependence instead of printing a dependable-looking hour unsupported by a dependable road.

archive_04_public_007.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_007.text: The public endowment terms required reasonable seasonal access to specific school and common-right records. They did not prescribe daily hours or free copies of every document. A later amendment authorised a small subsidy for readers unable to pay the copying fee. Luo had been using that subsidy informally, making poor visitors explain themselves at his desk. He said he disliked forms. Yue asked whether the visitors might dislike asking a favour even more. He turned the subsidy page toward her and sat quietly while she read it again.

archive_04_public_008.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_008.text: A recent recipient had permitted her application to be used in reviewing the scheme, with identifying details withheld. Her letter described borrowing a neighbour's coat so she would appear respectable enough to ask Luo for help. The copy fee had been waived readily. She nevertheless remembered the coat more vividly than the document. Luo recognised the consultation but agreed not to identify her from the description in the meeting. He drew a line through his proposed phrase simple discretionary kindness. A kindness could be offered easily and still cost its recipient the wrong kind of preparation.

archive_04_public_009.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_009.text: They drafted an announced waiver procedure based on the existing authority. It used a short self-declaration accepted by the designated steward, with reasons kept out of the public queue. The annual subsidy could fund only twenty standard sheets before review; the notice would state that limit and give a contact for further decisions. Luo wanted to omit the limit to avoid discouraging applicants. Dai insisted readers should know what could actually be offered. Yue proposed reporting remaining capacity privately at the request desk, so a public number would not reveal who had received help.

archive_04_public_010.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_010.text: The discussion grew sharp over a different problem. A visitor could need more than one sheet, and a twenty-sheet subsidy did not mean twenty people. Dai wanted the board to approve any allocation rule. Luo wanted to begin immediately for the next winter arrivals. They agreed to use the existing discretionary procedure until the board decided, while posting its existence in plain language. The draft rule remained a proposal. Yue copied proposed in the heading twice, once where an impatient clerk might cut off the top of the sheet for reuse.

archive_04_public_011.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_011.text: In the afternoon, an orchard worker asked to see the public school-path agreement. He was not the occupant of the disputed house and had no special role in the inheritance matter. He wanted to know whether a temporary fence could close the route during apple picking. Luo supplied the admitted public extract and explained where an access complaint belonged. The worker read slowly with one finger beside the lines. Yue waited without offering to translate his expression into distress. After a while he smiled because the school gate still had to remain reachable.

archive_04_public_012.speaker: lin_yue
archive_04_public_012.text: The clause is here, and I can copy the admitted words if you want to take them to the orchard steward. I do not know whether the planned fence actually blocks the route, because I have not seen its placement. If you describe it, we can add your question to the proper office's request. You should be able to ask what keeps the path open without joining a house claim or choosing which petitioner deserves to live beside it. Those are connected places, but different questions.

archive_04_public_013.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_013.text: The worker chose one standard extract and paid its posted fee. Luo recorded it as an ordinary consultation. The quiet transaction reassured Yue after the fraught inheritance sessions. Public records could help someone whose life was not about to become the archive's central drama. The worker left with the sheet tucked inside an apple crate lid, asking the clerk for a clean wrapper before he went into the drizzle. The practical request prevented a perfectly good extract from beginning its useful life soaked through.

archive_04_public_014.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_014.text: The council clerk's grant terms required a winter access schedule, not an attendance target. Luo admitted he had almost added a promised minimum number of visitors to make the application sound vigorous. Dai said an empty open room in bad weather could still satisfy its purpose if the people who needed it knew when to come. They selected three public sessions a week, one aligned with the cart, plus an enquiry channel for lawful urgent extracts during closures. The urgent channel depended on available transport and staff; it could not carry a reader through a blocked mountain.

archive_04_public_015.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_015.text: A local shopkeeper attended the planning meeting to object to the copying subsidy. He paid full fees and thought subsidised readers received a service he financed. Luo showed him the restricted endowment line that funded the subsidy separately from copy charges. The shopkeeper then asked whether someone receiving help could resell the extract. Dai explained that a standard certified extract served its named legal purpose and did not acquire extra authority by sale. She avoided inventing a broad punishment for the hypothetical transaction. The man seemed disappointed not to receive an outrage worth taking home.

archive_04_public_016.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_016.text: He did contribute a useful suggestion. The published schedule should name days in the valley market calendar as well as dates, because several cart passengers remembered the market cycle more reliably. Yue checked both systems with the clerk before adding them. The shopkeeper departed pleased with his own influence, and Luo kept the suggestion without attaching a moral lesson to it. A person could object badly to a subsidy and understand how neighbours found the mountain road. The report had room for that awkward combination.

archive_04_public_017.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_017.text: The endowment's emergency closure provision required three board members to confirm a closure lasting more than three consecutive scheduled sessions. Dai had once closed the hall for six sessions after a damp outbreak under her general custody authority. No papers had been damaged, and the precaution was sensible; the approval trail was incomplete. She added the episode to the proposed annual review rather than waiting for Luo to find it. Yue watched him receive this offered defect with less pleasure than she expected. It enlarged a responsibility they both had to repair.

archive_04_public_018.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_018.text: They prepared a closure notice form that gave a reason, likely review date and alternative enquiry contact. Its approval spaces followed the existing board rule. It could be completed quickly because the ordinary decisions had been thought through in advance. The form itself did not make an unsafe room openable. Tan checked that its wording left physical reopening to the carpenter or preservation lead appropriate to the cause. Yue took the clean draft to the cook, who said the contact line needed a location, because hungry people could not deliver an enquiry to a title.

archive_04_public_019.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_019.text: Luo laughed and added the lower receiving house as the message point, with the house clerk's prior agreement attached. He then asked Yue whether she thought public usefulness could save the archive from becoming afraid of its own deposits. She said usefulness had not found the house paper by itself; two custodians admitting different failures had helped. He looked wounded for a moment, then relieved. The report did not need to turn his cause into the cause of every good discovery. Its strongest pages described specific readers who could actually arrive.

archive_04_public_020.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_020.text: On the last afternoon of their route work, the teacher's daughter acknowledged receiving the further lender correction. She said the lender had removed the old note from her active reference. No warm thanks followed. Luo read the authorised update and smiled anyway. A practical consequence had finally travelled beyond the archive's own ledger. He placed the acknowledgement beside the dispatch receipts and marked the follow-up complete. Yue felt the difference between that word and closed. Another future request could open a different account without undoing what had been accomplished here.

archive_04_public_021.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_021.text: Their final public report contained a schedule, subsidy proposal, seasonal transport comparison, two failures and several successful alternatives. It recommended no opening of private family packets. Luo signed his own earlier copying failure in the catalogue section and left Dai's signature for her own entry. Yue signed only the comparisons she had actually performed. Before carrying the report to the board bundle, Luo removed the sentence he had written as a flourish at the end. Its place remained blank. The plain pages were strong enough to carry themselves.

archive_04_public_022.speaker: narrator
archive_04_public_022.text: When Yue finished with Luo, the roof workers had begun fixing the new beam seats. He was returning from a paid courier route, and Tan stood beside a covered trolley in the yard. They had been working on the other reports throughout the same days. Yue knew neither report's conclusions yet. She brought the public bundle to the common table and put it in the space marked for the board. The three spaces waited without ranking one form of work above another, though Luo's sheet corners were considerably tidier than his lunch apron.

archive_04_witness_001.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_001.text: He met Yue and the appointed clerk at the lower gate on the twentieth morning. His mother would join them at the school path, where she had agreed to identify work she remembered. The clerk carried a blank evidence sheet whose first fields concerned what each person had actually seen. He carried a spade for an unrelated paid drain-clearing task scheduled after the visit. He had argued to keep the task. A petitioner who needed his own wages should not have to become available every hour merely because people had started listening.

archive_04_witness_002.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_002.text: The path looked unremarkable in dry weather. Water still glinted under leaves in the cut drain, and the school gate had a scar where a cart axle once struck it. He's mother pointed to a stone she had reset after a spring flood. The clerk asked for a year. She named the season when the teacher's youngest pupil broke an arm, then said she could check her own household notebook for the date. The clerk wrote the remembered event as a lead. He did not turn the broken arm into an exact calendar day.

archive_04_witness_003.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_003.text: The school caretaker brought the ordinary repair book. Its entry named three neighbours clearing a blocked drain during that spring. He's mother's name appeared second. The work was real, publicly recorded and unpaid. The entry described a communal school task without mentioning the house tenancy condition. He wanted it labelled family maintenance immediately. The clerk said it established an action, while the deed's required relationship between action and right remained a legal question. Yue watched He push his thumb hard into the spade handle and then release it.

archive_04_witness_004.speaker: he_xi
archive_04_witness_004.text: I thought finding our names would feel like standing on solid ground. It feels as if the ground has a second layer someone else must approve. I do understand why the clerk cannot decide what the deed means. I am saying it aloud because if I keep every frustration inside my mouth, I will speak as if you invented it. Please record the school book fairly. My mother should not lose the fact of her work simply because it does not instantly finish the claim I hoped it would finish.

archive_04_witness_005.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_005.text: They found the retired neighbour at her daughter's house above the path. The woman agreed to discuss the drain clearance with the clerk and the two assistants. She declined to discuss the founder's final illness, which she had helped nurse. He had brought a question about whether the founder intended the house to remain with his grandmother's descendants. The neighbour said intentions she remembered from sickroom talk were not part of today's offer. She was willing to name a shovel, a flood and who stood in water beside her.

archive_04_witness_006.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_006.text: Her recollection differed from He's mother's on the stone. The mother had reset it after the clearance, not during the main morning's work. The difference did not make either account useless. The clerk separated the two actions and asked whether the school book might record only one. The neighbour laughed at the thought of the old caretaker writing down every stone. He had complained that the women stopped to warm their feet at his stove, she said. She remembered that because he later brought them hot water without being asked.

archive_04_witness_007.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_007.text: Yue looked down at the woman's present swollen ankles. The witness had accepted the agreed travel and time payment to come to the later hearing if it happened while the road remained safe. The payment was for attendance, not for supporting a particular account. The clerk read that condition aloud and recorded the amount in the district witness request. He asked whether the widow's daughter could accompany her. That additional travel would require approval. She did not agree to wait on the mountain all winter merely to save someone the trouble of scheduling.

archive_04_witness_008.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_008.text: The second neighbour had moved to the valley kiln settlement. He said the morning path work preceded the trustee's trench repair, while the orchard invoice dated its trench earlier. Yue put the two dates on separate slips. The man thought for a while and corrected himself: he had helped clear the path twice, once before the trench and once afterwards. His first memory joined the two mornings because both had begun with the same broken cart. The clerk kept the correction visible rather than replacing the initial statement with a smoother story.

archive_04_witness_009.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_009.text: The ordinary kiln wage ledger helped date his later visit. He had missed a morning's firing shift with permission for school work, and the ledger recorded the reason because another worker received the replacement pay. He offered the relevant entry after the clerk explained its use. The rest of the wage page remained covered. Yue copied a date and the stated reason, not neighbouring workers' earnings. The former neighbour seemed relieved that helping He's mother did not require bringing an entire workshop's accounts into the house dispute.

archive_04_witness_010.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_010.text: On the return walk, He said it was embarrassing that the best date came from someone else's paid replacement. His mother had lost time without an employer recording it, so her work depended on witnesses and a school book. Yue thought of the apprentice's unreadable birth date and answered that the record system favoured actions which disturbed an account. A task performed quietly could be no less necessary. They could identify that disadvantage in the hearing's evidence summary without inventing a wage entry for work nobody had paid.

archive_04_witness_011.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_011.text: The current orchard worker in the disputed house invited the clerk to his door after receiving formal notice. He declined He and Yue as listeners for his personal circumstances, allowing the clerk alone. They waited outside near the gate rather than treating refusal as hostility. Yue heard a kettle set down but no words. He watched the house wall with an expression she could not read. A pot of herbs stood where his grandmother had once grown beans. The ordinary alteration seemed to hurt more than the trustees' account of roof money.

archive_04_witness_012.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_012.text: When the clerk came out, he gave only the agreed procedural update: the occupant had accepted notice, appointed a contact and would submit relevant rent receipts. He had not agreed to publish his health or income. He nodded as if he had expected more and knew why he should not receive it. They passed the school gate again without stopping. Later he asked Yue whether a person could be both the obstacle between him and his grandmother's house and someone who deserved a home. She said the hearing would be poorer if it forgot either fact.

archive_04_witness_013.speaker: lin_yue
archive_04_witness_013.text: I cannot make those needs fit by deciding which person I like. I can help keep the records from shrinking either of you into a problem to remove. Your family has a documented enquiry that went unanswered properly. The present occupant has a life in the house now. If the deed gives you a right, someone will still need to decide how that right is carried out lawfully. That may be slower than the word yours sounds. Slowness can be unfair, but haste can injure someone too.

archive_04_witness_014.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_014.text: He completed his paid drain task that afternoon. The task belonged to the school caretaker's current work order, with wages already authorised from maintenance funds. He asked the clerk to record it separately from the inherited condition evidence. He did not want a new paid shovel stroke to appear as proof of an unpaid childhood history. Yue helped the clerk check the work order reference and then left him to his job. It was the first time He had made the distinction before anyone required him to, and he looked irritated by how satisfied it made him.

archive_04_witness_015.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_015.text: The path drain revealed a pottery shard stamped with a school kitchen mark. He handed it to the caretaker rather than announcing an ancestral discovery. The caretaker said children regularly broke bowls near the gate and saved the shard for ordinary disposal. Yue laughed with him. After several days in which every object threatened to become evidence, the broken bowl's lack of importance felt like rest. He said his grandmother would have approved. Then he stopped, smiled at his own habit and put the spade back into the wet ground.

archive_04_witness_016.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_016.text: Sun declined the proposed broad testimony about the founder's character. She had known him at public school meetings, not as a person arranging house inheritance. She would confirm her own attendance at one meeting if the minutes required clarification, after receiving the exact question. He accepted the refusal and removed a sentence from his witness request that called her the village's living memory. She thanked him for removing it. The phrase had made her feel like an overfilled shelf nobody intended to repair.

archive_04_witness_017.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_017.text: She did offer a lead on the path agreement. The school had hung a public copy beside its gate for several years, and the teacher had referred to it when orchard carts blocked the entrance. Sun remembered an ink stain over a particular word but not whether it said occupant or descendants. A former pupil now worked at the district registry and might remember where the notice had been returned. The clerk recorded the possible source and sent an ordinary request through the registry channel. He did not ask Sun to strengthen a word her memory had blurred.

archive_04_witness_018.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_018.text: The orchard representative provided a work book showing trustees paying for annual pruning and ditch maintenance. Several entries described shared school access, including one paid repair after the family's earlier request. These records supported real expenditure without proving the trustees held every asserted right. Yue copied the agreed fields while the representative kept unrelated harvest accounts closed. He read the resulting extracts and admitted that the path had not been maintained only by his family. His mother agreed. Neither withdrew the years when their names and work were independently recorded.

archive_04_witness_019.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_019.text: The clerk's summary therefore separated routine unpaid clearance, paid structural repair and later courier labour. Its legal question asked whether the inherited condition required exclusive maintenance or participation in a shared obligation. That interpretation would belong to the registrar or the proper hearing body. The summary did not choose one by calling all work the same word. He found the distinction exhausting. His mother said it looked more like the path she knew: everyone using it, different people fixing different pieces, and arguments when nobody wanted the last muddy task.

archive_04_witness_020.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_020.text: A witness from the orchard remembered He's grandmother accepting rent-free occupation in return for keeping the school gate unblocked. Another remembered the founder promising her family security after decades of work. The clerk accepted each statement within the witness's agreed scope and noted that neither person had seen the later revision completed. Yue did not ask whose affection was purer. A promise of security and a practical duty could have belonged to the same arrangement. Their coexistence was a reason to examine the instrument carefully, not an excuse to discard whichever memory complicated a favourite outcome.

archive_04_witness_021.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_021.text: He and his mother reviewed the statement fields they would submit. She removed a sentence suggesting that the trustees had always treated them with contempt. Some had brought food during an illness; one had denied the house without reading the later clause. The removed sentence would have been easier to repeat in anger than the surviving particulars. He watched her make the change and said his father would dislike the softened account. She answered that it had become more exact, and that exactness could be hard enough without borrowing another person's cruelty.

archive_04_witness_022.speaker: narrator
archive_04_witness_022.text: At the end of the route work, Yue carried the bounded witness summary to the archive while He returned to his paid road. The clerk retained the signed originals under the agreed district case procedure. The board report contained only the information needed for scheduling, witness travel and public path obligations, withholding private household testimony. Luo had his public access pages ready, and Tan's covered trolley waited beside the roof works. Yue set her limited report among theirs. The school drain still carried rain below the gate, a practical fact no column had created.

archive_04_preserve_001.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_001.text: Tan began their winter preparation route by taking Yue to the empty northern bay. The beam supports were already in place, and the room remained closed to ordinary visitors. Rain showed as dark threads along the damaged joint, separate from the buckets below. Tan pointed out the temporary repair's successes first: shelves dry, walking boards sound and runoff directed away from the door. Then she showed the joint that still opened when the roof moved. Winter snow would give it a different load. A tidy bucket could not bargain with that weight.

archive_04_preserve_002.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_002.text: The carpenter had ordered two replacement beam lengths, each cut for its named span. One arrived with a deep knot near the intended bearing. It met the merchant's general timber grade but failed the carpenter's specified load requirement. He rejected that length before installation and attached the order wording to the refusal. The supplier's agreed replacement terms covered the return cart and new timber. Yue helped label the rejected beam so an impatient worker would not choose it merely because it was already inside the yard.

archive_04_preserve_003.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_003.text: The rejection delayed the northern span by two days. Luo wanted to open the southern public tables during those days, but the longer timber handling route would cross their exit. Tan refused simultaneous use. Dai approved a changed public session in the lower receiving room, using copies that could travel safely. Yue wrote the temporary arrangement on the notice and watched a visitor read it without becoming angry. The visitor had come for one grazing extract and preferred a lower room to a roof worth arguing about.

archive_04_preserve_004.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_004.text: A younger roof worker asked whether Yue could hold the rejected beam with qi while he trimmed around the knot. She asked the carpenter what the beam would become after trimming. It would be too short for either approved span and could serve only a later small ordinary repair. The powered hold would therefore expose people to a pointless risk. The worker looked sheepish and carried the beam back onto its dry supports with the others. Stage five had not changed the timber's length or the load the joint required.

archive_04_preserve_005.speaker: tan_ke
archive_04_preserve_005.text: I know why he asked. People see four opened pairs and imagine spare strength waiting to be assigned. They cannot see the training, delivery path and load calculation as clearly as they see your hands. Sometimes I am guilty of a similar hope when I see a preservation tool. I imagine the page after treatment before asking whether the tool suits this ink. Today we have a beam that does not belong in the span. Calling it an opportunity would only make the wrong piece harder to refuse.

archive_04_preserve_006.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_006.text: They measured the safe shelf capacity using the carpenter's existing load marks and Tan's packet weights. A winter move needed more than room for the current boxes. It needed an aisle wide enough for a supported trolley, a place to inspect arrivals and a separate surface for damp items. Yue drew the spaces on a plan, then walked the actual turns with an empty trolley. One corner required a cabinet to move before winter, while the floor was dry and the cabinet's owner list could be checked without an emergency behind them.

archive_04_preserve_007.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_007.text: The cabinet held public reference copies, not entrusted originals. Dai authorised its move after the titles and count were verified. Two workers lifted the empty sections over sound boards while Yue guided the cleared doorway. The rearrangement uncovered a mouse nest in an unused base compartment. Tan halted the move, isolated the dirty compartment and asked the ordinary pest worker to inspect adjacent spaces. None of the clean reference copies showed damage. Relief came with a new inspection task rather than permission to pretend the nest had never been there.

archive_04_preserve_008.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_008.text: The pest worker found two old entry gaps in the wall plaster and one current route beneath the pantry sill. Repairing the gaps required ordinary mortar and a fitted sill plate, not a stronger preservation charm. The pantry would remain separately checked while the work dried. The cook was furious about a scoop left on the floor by a previous shift. She put a clean scoop on a hanging hook and made everyone demonstrate that they could reach it. Yue failed the first demonstration because she laughed, which made the cook even more exacting.

archive_04_preserve_009.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_009.text: The winter fuel store contained twenty-eight sound sacks of dry charcoal, each checked at five kilograms. Three damp sacks were excluded from the heating stock pending the supplier's agreed inspection. Tan did not count them as half-useful merely because someone hoped they would dry in time. The heater technician's ordinary tests used one sound sack for a cold day's common hall heat and half a sack for a milder day at the planned occupied area. Closing unused bays reduced the heated space. It did not make cold paper or cold people disappear.

archive_04_preserve_010.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_010.text: Yue helped compare the test record with the proposed winter schedule. Seventy-two cold days and twenty-four milder days would require eighty-four sacks before contingency. A target stock of ninety-six sound sacks left twelve beyond that planning allowance. The archive would need sixty-eight additional accepted sacks to reach it, apart from the disputed damp ones. The figures were provisional until the board approved the winter programme. Tan wrote the assumptions beside the numbers, because a long cold spell could spend the reserve faster than a neat column suggested.

archive_04_preserve_011.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_011.text: The heater technician inspected the common hall's safe small brazier and its flue path. A drying cabinet used a different controlled supply and could not be silently added to the hall's fuel allowance. Tan wanted to run cabinet treatment only when qualified staff and its separate treatment budget were available, prioritising damaged items already assessed. Yue helped mark the distinction on the room plan. Public readers would see a warm hall. They would not be invited to assume that every sealed cabinet behind the screen shared its heat.

archive_04_preserve_012.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_012.text: The sealed winter pantry counted food through the cook's established daily kitchen share: measured grain, beans, oil and dried vegetables sufficient for one ordinary adult day's meals under the kitchen plan. Its stored usable components supplied three hundred and forty shares. The winter target was one thousand and sixty, requiring seven hundred and twenty more. At ten regular residents for ninety-six days, the planned consumption would be nine hundred and sixty, leaving one hundred shares for delay or admitted emergency guests. The cook insisted that visitors eating lunch be entered too; a polite bowl still came from a finite pot.

archive_04_preserve_013.speaker: tan_ke
archive_04_preserve_013.text: The cold and food allowances do not run at the same pace. Two extra people use two daily shares even on a mild day when the hall burns only half a sack. A colder empty room can use more fuel without feeding anyone else. I want the board to understand that before it calls our supplies ninety-six days and stops thinking. We have quantities and assumptions, not a promise that weather will behave. Your plan should leave a place to write what the days actually take.

archive_04_preserve_014.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_014.text: The supply offers were itemised. Accepted charcoal, food components and their ordinary cart delivery together would cost six hundred copper under the current quotes. The exact component quantities followed the kitchen and heater calculations; the total did not authorise substitutes chosen for convenience. A supplier could return damp fuel or short food sacks rather than turning the archive's reserve into a dispute about appearance. Dai requested the offer dates before presenting the winter reserve plan to the board. Yue copied them beside the quantities, where a purchasing clerk would see both.

archive_04_preserve_015.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_015.text: Tan then taught Yue to distinguish a damp cover from a wet text block by inspection under support. The lesson used discarded practice material, not a family's irreplaceable page. Yue recorded what she could see and what required opening by a qualified hand. On her first attempt she confidently called the inner leaves dry because the outer edge was pale. Tan opened the practice sample and showed a wet centre. Yue laughed at herself, then wrote a better description. Confidence had been useful only after it survived correction.

archive_04_preserve_016.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_016.text: They rehearsed a winter leak response with empty boxes. One person called the location, another closed the safe approach and the designated handling lead chose which authorised objects could move. Yue practised moving a supported empty tray through the newly cleared aisle. The first drill exposed a turn where the door latch caught a sleeve. The carpenter filed the latch and checked its closure again. The second drill went faster without anyone having to hurry. Tan valued the ordinary improvement more than a spectacular rescue that existed only in imagination.

archive_04_preserve_017.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_017.text: Dai brought the deposit terms for packets near the repaired span. Several allowed temporary movement within the archive after notice; two required an owner's reply unless immediate danger justified emergency relocation. Both owners still had reachable autumn addresses. Dai sent the notices before the road worsened and prepared alternative safe support positions while waiting. Yue worked from packet numbers without reading their private contents. This was practical preparation, but Dai's face showed something less mechanical: she wanted the owners to find that their careful instructions had mattered in a season of pressure.

archive_04_preserve_018.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_018.text: One owner replied the next day allowing the move under a sealed wrapper and requesting a condition report. The other asked whether the work could wait until a relative arrived in four days. The carpenter could finish the permitted adjoining work first without compromising the support schedule. Dai accepted the delay and sent a reply naming the revised handling time. Luo grumbled about lost efficiency, then checked the public opening calendar and found the delay could serve the same temporary room arrangement. A private owner's request had shifted work rather than defeated it.

archive_04_preserve_019.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_019.text: A small accident in the yard tested the cleared route. A slate slipped from a worker's grip and shattered beside the trolley wheel. Nobody was struck, but the fragments blocked the archive's planned packet exit. Yue stopped the empty tray rehearsal while the worker swept and the foreman inspected the stack restraint. Tan recorded the interruption. The worker apologised repeatedly until the foreman told him to help correct the restraint. An apology could begin safety work; it could not replace the strap that should have stopped the slate.

archive_04_preserve_020.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_020.text: The crew moved the slate stack farther from the exit and marked a separate unloading strip. The carter checked it against his turning space before agreeing. Yue redrew the movement plan once, not three times to preserve every person's first preference. The final sheet held the accepted route, the required stack restraint and the inspection responsibility. Tan stored the earlier draft as superseded rather than leaving it pinned beside the new plan. Two plausible routes posted together would give a frightened person one more question at exactly the wrong moment.

archive_04_preserve_021.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_021.text: They finished with the winter sleeping rooms. Ten ordinary residents could be accommodated without blocking the hall exit, including Yue if a separate renewal was agreed. Two further temporary places were possible in the receiving room, with bedding already held for travellers. Those places increased daily food use and could not become unrecorded permanent beds. The cook chose a simple arrival sheet kept in her kitchen, matched to the steward's guest book. She wanted to know whose breakfast she was making without waiting for a dispute about whether the guest counted as official.

archive_04_preserve_022.speaker: narrator
archive_04_preserve_022.text: Yue took Tan's preservation report to the common table at the end of the route work. It contained a safe movement plan, inspected room limits, sound fuel counts, kitchen shares, supplier dates and the beam replacement delay. It claimed no recovered text and no winter weather guarantee. Luo had pages ready about readers and public hours; the clerk had bounded path evidence and witness travel questions. He was still working a paid route below. Yue set the practical report in its marked place and looked at the three bundles together, relieved that none pretended to describe the whole mountain.

archive_04_shared_001.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_001.text: The governing board assembled on the twenty-sixth day of Yue's appointment. Its ordinary members included the school trustee and two mountain residents who had no role in the house claim. The orchard representative attended for the public path questions but did not vote on archive expenditure. He came only for the part of the meeting where his report contact was needed. Dai placed all three work bundles on the table and asked the staff leads to give their findings. Yue listened to the reports she had not helped prepare.

archive_04_shared_002.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_002.text: Luo described the winter public schedule, the cart timetable mismatch and the proposed copying subsidy procedure. He included the earlier closure approval failure and his own unanswered enquiry follow-up. The clerk described bounded path evidence without reading private household accounts into the room. Tan explained the rejected beam, accepted replacement terms and winter stock calculations. Each speaker identified the work completed and the points still dependent on outside decisions. By the time the first board member asked a question, Yue could finally see how the three reports met without becoming one account.

archive_04_shared_003.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_003.text: The member responsible for village stores objected to ninety-six days of provision. Winter isolation usually lasted less than that, and food held on the mountain could not be lent to hungry neighbours below. Tan showed the ten-resident baseline and the hundred additional kitchen shares. Luo showed the public duties that would continue during accessible weeks. The board member asked whether the archive might close completely and send everyone home before snow. Dai answered that nine staff homes lay at or beside the mountain, and closed doors would not give their winter needs to someone else.

archive_04_shared_004.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_004.text: The cook, invited for the food calculation, said her kitchen would happily serve fewer people if there were fewer people. She would not serve ten people from a figure written for seven. A nervous clerk laughed and then stopped when she looked at him. The board discussed purchase timing and storage inspection rather than asking her to stretch the same pot indefinitely. Yue found the sternness comforting. In many travelling kitchens she had seen generosity treated as an invisible supply. Here someone had given it a measuring bowl.

archive_04_shared_005.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_005.text: The winter operational reserve held one thousand four hundred and forty copper, separate from permanent staff's annual base wages and the restricted roof accounts. The board approved six hundred for the quoted fuel, food and cart deliveries. It provisionally set aside four hundred and eighty for a new ninety-six-calendar-day appointment at Yue's five-copper rate, including weekly rest, subject to her acceptance before her current term ended. Two hundred covered separately authorised qualified preservation and road work. One hundred and sixty remained uncommitted contingency. Dai read the four amounts twice; together they exhausted the reserve.

archive_04_shared_006.speaker: lin_yue
archive_04_shared_006.text: I will consider the renewal before my present term ends. Please do not count me as having accepted tonight because I have stayed for the meeting. I want to understand the winter duties, the rest schedule and what happens if the road closes beyond the appointment. I am willing to keep doing this work, but willingness becomes easier to trust when it has an end date. If I accept the ninety-six days, I will use the same five-copper rate and the written winter duties we agree.

archive_04_shared_007.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_007.text: The board reserved the money. Its ten-person winter baseline meant the nine resident staff and Yue after an accepted renewal. A member asked whether stage-five training meant Yue could replace a hired heater technician during an emergency. Tan answered before Yue had to defend herself: the heater's qualified inspection and flue work remained skilled ordinary duties. Yue's accepted controls covered bounded tested sockets, not arbitrary fuel savings or roof loads. The member withdrew the suggestion. The two-hundred work allowance remained available for real expertise instead of being cut because one worker carried a sword.

archive_04_shared_008.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_008.text: They approved the seasonal access schedule and required a review after four weeks of use. The subsidy rule was amended to let the steward offer up to two standard sheets per application within the twenty-sheet annual allocation, with further needs brought to the designated board contact. That rule did not guarantee ten people would each receive two sheets; actual use would be tracked. Luo accepted the ordinary arithmetic without trying to hide it under his preferred language of welcome. The cook asked whether the new contact had agreed to be contacted. He had.

archive_04_shared_009.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_009.text: A more difficult decision concerned the catalogue failure. The board appointed the visiting council clerk and an ordinary archive assistant to check the house paper's restored movement trail and the next ten old transfer entries. Dai would cooperate without approving her own review. Luo's desk handling would be reviewed on the same basis. The board refused a proposal to publish private accession contents merely to prove candour. A public summary could name procedural failures and correction steps; individual deposits would remain under their own access terms. Accountability did not require every owner to pay with exposure.

archive_04_shared_010.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_010.text: He joined the meeting when the clerk summarised witness timing. Two willing witnesses expected to leave the mountain district within eighteen days. Their limited statements could be signed now and submitted through the registrar's agreed process, while travel support for a later hearing would require a decision when the date was known. He asked whether winter closure would force his family to begin again in spring. The board could not bind the registrar. It could preserve the submitted sources and maintain the case correspondence so the mountain's closed road would not erase them.

archive_04_shared_011.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_011.text: The representative confirmed that the current house occupant had received notice and appointed a contact. His private circumstances were withheld. She asked that no public archive summary imply a settled right of repossession while the revision trail remained unresolved. He accepted that wording after asking the summary to acknowledge the recovered descendant clause. The clerk proposed a sentence naming both: a relevant endorsed instrument had been recovered, and its later legal status was under registry inquiry. Neither party liked every word. Both agreed it was a fact they could defend.

archive_04_shared_012.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_012.text: Sun arrived after the voting because the cook had promised her the pickle recipe. She found a room full of people trying to make a final sentence shorter. She said she had no authority over their sentence and waited by the kitchen door. Yue smiled at her and was rewarded with an exaggerated look of exhaustion. Later Sun would receive the specific meeting question she had agreed to consider, but tonight she was a visitor carrying a clean jar. Her ordinary errand survived the institution's appetite for useful old people.

archive_04_shared_013.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_013.text: The board authorised the supply orders while the offers remained valid. Dai and the designated purchasing member signed the quantities and inspection conditions. The clerk entered six hundred as committed, leaving the provisional appointment money reserved and the qualified-work amount untouched until tasks were approved. The charcoal order specified sixty-eight accepted dry five-kilogram sacks beyond the twenty-eight already sound. Food components would add seven hundred and twenty kitchen shares to the existing three hundred and forty. Disputed damp fuel stayed outside the stock count pending its separate return decision.

archive_04_shared_014.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_014.text: Delivery would come in three ordinary cart loads over the next week, subject to the inspected mountain route. A failed load would not become present stock because its invoice had been signed below. Tan and the cook would count and inspect arrivals before Dai accepted them. Yue copied the expected delivery dates on the store sheet, leaving the received column blank. The empty spaces felt deliberate rather than deficient. They showed exactly where the coming weather could interrupt the board's neat programme and require a different answer.

archive_04_shared_015.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_015.text: The winter pantry belonged to the coming programme, with sealed stocks kept apart from food bought for the current autumn kitchen. The cook would open it on the recorded starting day and count every issue thereafter. Current meals continued under the already funded autumn account. She marked the distinction on both shelves before anyone could admire a generous total that included food they intended to eat twice. Yue copied the starting-day field into the store book and left it blank until the programme was scheduled.

archive_04_shared_016.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_016.text: After the members left, Luo rolled the corrected mountain screen back into its corner. Dai gathered the budget pages, then paused to thank the cook for speaking plainly. The cook said she had been speaking plainly for twenty years and was delighted that a budget had finally noticed. Tan laughed hard enough to make the clerk look up. He put down his pen and laughed too. Yue realised how long the room had held itself carefully upright. The relief did not settle the house claim, but it gave them enough breath to return to it.

archive_04_shared_017.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_017.text: The district registrar's first reply arrived at evening. The later revision request had indeed been filed, but the completion record had a disputed cross-reference to an orchard settlement rather than a simple revocation. The registrar would need the recovered instrument's certified extract and the existing occupant's notice record before arranging the formal comparison. The letter asked for two witnesses whose names appeared on the revision application. One was dead. The other was a retired boundary clerk living beyond the ridge, where autumn rain had damaged the safest road.

archive_04_shared_018.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_018.text: Dai placed the letter beside the board's approved winter plan. The supplies had a route, the house evidence had another, and both depended on weather that could make a tidy timetable meaningless. He read the retired clerk's name and said he could reach the village on his ordinary courier circuit if the repaired bridge reopened. Luo began to ask him to leave at dawn, then asked for the route assessment instead. The small correction was visible to everyone. A family claim did not turn its petitioner into an inexhaustible messenger.

archive_04_shared_019.speaker: narrator
archive_04_shared_019.text: Yue left the table with three reports now part of a common plan and one new letter asking for a person beyond the ridge. The roof replacement had begun, the winter purchases were authorised and her renewal remained a decision she could still make. Outside, wet leaves blocked the yard's upper drain. She called the duty worker and helped mark the spot for the morning clearance rather than slipping into an unassigned night task. The mountain had become a place she might stay. It had not become a place where every need was hers to absorb.
